findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer plainly what Athena is and what makes it different. This is the strongest part of the page for this reader.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.

findings.text: The page says why it exists: it is a demonstration. But almost everything after the header is about firstmate, so a newcomer who came to learn about Athena learns little more about it after the first three paragraphs.
findings.source: Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim, and every claim to lines in the project's own files.

findings.text: A next-step link near the top, and a 'Next steps' section with a repo link and two commands, make it clear what to do next.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself.

findings.text: The install step assumes the reader already has a checkout. It gives no clone command and names no prerequisites, such as a Rust toolchain or model access, so a newcomer has to go to the repo before they can try anything.
findings.source: Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh

findings.text: The header promises that Athena shows how it read the request, uses a second model to check the work, and records costs. Nothing on this page shows any of these, so the newcomer has to take those selling points on trust.

Most of the page is a dense state machine with 44 cited claims, full of firstmate terms such as yolo, secondmate, exit 75 and places-held. A newcomer to Athena will likely skim or leave here. The 'Start here' section and the glossary help, but the detail is aimed at someone already evaluating firstmate.

'Limits of this study' mentions details of how the study was made, such as a first reading that missed paths. It also points to internal folders ('the name of the folder under studies/'). Neither means anything to a first-time reader, and admitting a missed first pass may make the reader trust the demonstration less.
findings.source: f3 ... A first reading of the pinned tree missed these paths: teardown reopening a backlog item (t9, c23 to c25), ...

findings.text: 'Start here' says three parts follow, but a fourth part, 'Words used first', comes before them. This is a small mismatch in a section meant to orient the reader.
findings.source: The three parts below say what firstmate is, follow one piece of work, and say what happens when something fails or has no limit.

findings.text: Every statement links to a claim, and every claim links to exact lines at a pinned commit. A reader can check any statement, which shows the traceability Athena advertises.
findings.source: Each statement below ends with the id of the claim that supports it; the claims, with links to their sources, are listed at the end.
